overview: Prakriti-bandha refers to the binding of karma to the soul, specifically regarding the type, nature, and characteristics of karmic particles that attach to the soul. In Jain philosophy, karma is not merely an abstract concept but a physical substance that interacts with the soul. Prakriti-bandha describes how different categories of karma influence the soul's qualities and life experiences. These karmas are classified into eight main categories: Jñānāvaraṇīya (Knowledge-obscuring), Darśanāvaraṇīya (Perception-obscuring), Vedanīya (Feeling-producing), Mohanīya (Deluding), Āyu (Life-span determining), Nāma (Physique-determining), Gotra (Status-determining), and Antarāya (Obstructive). Each of these categories affects the soul in specific ways, altering its purity and influencing its journey towards liberation. Understanding Prakriti-bandha is essential for practitioners as it highlights the importance of conscious actions and spiritual discipline in mitigating karmic accumulation.

primary_sources.title: Tattvārthasūtra
primary_sources.author: Acharya Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: The nature of karmic bondage is understood.
primary_sources.notes: The Tattvārthasūtra is a foundational Jain text that elaborates on the nature of reality, including the mechanism of karma and its effects on the soul.

misconceptions.myth: Prakriti-bandha means the soul is permanently tainted by karma.
misconceptions.reality: In Jainism, the soul is inherently pure, and karma is an external substance that can be shed through right knowledge, faith, and conduct.
